summary.intent: Improve the `entire insights` and `entire improve` CLI commands to be more useful: fix zero scores, add on-demand summary backfill, fix improve's pattern detection, and add tool/skill usage tracking to insights.
summary.outcome: All goals achieved: scores now have meaningful variance (6.7–47.3), backfill generates summaries on demand, improve uses keyword-theme matching instead of exact-match SQL, tool call tracking was added to insights, and all tests pass.

repo: Summarization runs as a post-commit hook via `summarize/claude.go` and stores structured JSON (intent, outcome, friction, learnings) in checkpoint metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
The insights SQLite cache is populated from checkpoint metadata; friction and learnings only exist if summarize ran, making backfill necessary for older sessions.

`QueryRecurringFriction` uses exact-text SQL matching — it never finds duplicates because friction strings are unique sentences. `AnalyzePatterns` uses keyword-theme grouping and is the correct approach for `entire improve`.
`nullableFloat` was used for score columns, making 0.0 indistinguishable from NULL (not computed) — replaced with direct float storage + `has_summary` boolean.

Token efficiency score was broken: formula assumed ~8k tokens/file but real sessions use 300k–6M tokens/file, causing the dimension to always score 0. Fixed by basing efficiency on tokens-per-turn with a log curve.
`gofmt` repeatedly strips trailing `//nolint:ireturn` comments from function signatures in `agent/capabilities.go` — these must be placed on the line above the return statement.
The `nolint` directive requires the specific linter name and an explanation text to satisfy `nolintlint` (e.g., `//nolint:ireturn // interface needed for capability registry`).
Condensed transcripts have `Entry.ToolName` and `Entry.ToolDetail` fields usable for extracting per-session tool call counts during cache refresh.
`llmcli.Runner` shells out to `claude --print` and the JSON response includes `total_cost_usd` and `usage` fields — these were previously discarded but now returned as `UsageInfo`.

code.finding: All four scoring dimensions were recalibrated: token efficiency now uses log(tokens)/turns, first-pass baseline is 90 with turn-based penalties, friction penalty is 15 per point, and focus uses a gaussian curve on files/turns ratio.
Execute now returns (string, *UsageInfo, error) where UsageInfo contains InputTokens, OutputTokens, and TotalCostUSD parsed from the claude CLI JSON response.

runImprove now uses AnalyzePatterns (keyword themes) for both dry-run and full-run instead of QueryRecurringFriction (exact match). attachTranscriptExcerpts now uses AffectedSessions from the pattern directly.
InsertSession now calls insertToolCalls to store per-session tool usage counts. UpdateSessionSummary added for backfill path. has_summary column tracks which sessions have been summarized.

backfillSummaries function added: queries sessions without summaries, generates them via Claude, and updates the cache. metadataToSessionRow now calls extractToolCounts to count tool usage from condensed transcript entries.
ComputeAgentComparisons now aggregates tool call counts across sessions and computes TopTools and AvgToolCalls per agent comparison.
Theme keywords expanded with real-world patterns (api_error, ci_failure, merge_conflict, test_flake, lint, compile, auth, timeout, review, context). maxFrictionExamples = 10 cap added.

workflow: When gofmt strips nolint comments from long lines, place the directive on the line above rather than inline on the function signature.
Exact-match SQL grouping is the wrong approach for natural language friction strings — keyword-theme classification is needed to surface recurring problems.
When adding a new DB column, always bump the schema version and handle the migration so existing caches don't break.
The `nullableFloat` pattern for scores creates an ambiguity between 'scored zero' and 'not scored' — use a separate boolean column instead.
Test scorer formulas against real data distributions before shipping — abstract unit tests can pass while the formula is broken against actual values.

friction: `gofmt` repeatedly stripped `//nolint:ireturn` comments from `agent/capabilities.go`, requiring multiple re-add attempts across commits.
The simplify commit (`4c095d6e`) did not actually include the `capabilities.go` nolint fix, causing lint failures to resurface in the next session.
`replace_all` on a function name accidentally renamed the function definition itself in addition to call sites, requiring a manual fix.

Recent sessions had no summaries (summarization was just enabled), so initial `entire insights` and `entire improve` runs returned all zeros and no patterns — required implementing backfill before the feature could be tested.
`entire improve --dry-run` returned 0 patterns even with 21 friction points because `QueryRecurringFriction` used exact-text SQL matching on unique natural language strings.
Merge conflict in `manual_commit_condensation.go` between branch's session scoring block and main's `writeOpts` variable + v2 dual-write required manual resolution.
open_items: `SessionRow.CacheTokens` field is declared but never populated.
Stringly-typed status/priority/direction values across packages would benefit from typed constants.
N+1 query pattern in `insightsdb/queries.go` (`populateDenormalized`) — 3 extra queries per session row.
`TotalTokens` lives in `termstyle` (presentation package) but is a data computation — ideally should live in `agent` or a utility package.
`statusStyles` wrapper in `status_style.go` adds indirection over `termstyle.Styles` — could be removed but requires refactoring `status.go`.
Trend computation compares arbitrary halves of sessions which isn't statistically meaningful for small N — needs minimum session count guard.
Tool call tracking was added to the DB and insights display, but `UpdateSessionSummary` (backfill path) does not re-extract tool counts for backfilled sessions — only new sessions get tool counts.
The `improve` friction theme keywords are manually maintained — consider deriving them from actual friction data or using embedding-based clustering.
